title: Classic Sauce Espagnole
description: The classic brown mother sauce: brown veal or beef stock, brown roux, mirepoix, and tomato. A savory foundation for other brown sauces.
ingredients: 50 g clarified butter, divided: 35 g for roux and 15 g for vegetables
1.25 L unsalted brown veal or beef stock, plus a little extra as needed
steps: In a heavy saucepan, heat 35 g clarified butter. Stir in the flour and cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until evenly nut brown, about 10–15 minutes. Do not scorch it; discard and restart if burnt.
In a separate pan, heat the remaining 15 g butter. Brown the onion, carrot, and celery for 8–10 minutes. Add tomato paste and cook 2 minutes, until brick red.
Take the roux off the heat briefly. Gradually whisk in the stock until smooth, then add the browned vegetables, tomato paste, herbs, and peppercorns.

Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook uncovered for 60–90 minutes, stirring along the bottom and skimming fat and foam. Aim for about 750 mL and a sauce that lightly coats a spoon; add stock if it gets too thick before the flour flavor cooks out.
Strain through a fine sieve without forcing the vegetables through. Adjust consistency with stock or gentle reduction. Salt only after reduction.
notes: Use unsalted, well made brown stock; ordinary salty broth becomes too salty when reduced. Espagnole is usually a foundation for finished sauces, rather than a heavily seasoned table sauce. Pair finished brown sauces with beef, roasted meats, or mushrooms. For a traditional demi-glace approach, combine equal volumes espagnole and brown stock and reduce by about half. Stock-making time is not included.
